156646.overview: Assuming the role of Special Forces Operative Roy Adams, the player attempts to rescue five hostages who are being held captive in enemy territory. The game is divided into six stages, each of which advances the story when completed. For example, after the Jungle stage is completed, Adams interrogates an enemy soldier and learns the location of the concentration camp where the hostages are being held. This was one of the first shooter games to feature a storyline.

188814.overview: Ougon no Rashinban: Shouyou Maru San Francisco Kouro Satsujin Jiken is an Adventure game, developed and published by Riverhillsoft, which was released in Japan in 1991

192862.overview: A Japanese teenager named Hiroki is interested in martial arts, and has to take care of his little sister. Their older brother Yoichi had gone abroad; just when he announced that he was coming back he disappeared under mysterious circumstances. Hiroki and his friends eventually find out that an international supernatural criminal syndicate is in cohorts with an even darker power that is about to bring the apocalypse onto Earth. Only You can be considered a hybrid of RPG and visual novel-like adventure with choices that affect the storyline and the hero's relationship with various female characters. Locations are represented as still anime-style images, and all the interaction is done with menu commands. Much of the gameplay is dedicated to selecting locations from a city map and triggering extended cutscenes. The RPG elements are present in scripted and random one-on-one turn-based battles, during which Hiroki and his opponent exchange various types of physical and special attacks until one of them is defeated. The protagonist gains experience points from battles and levels up. There are no equipment or usable items in the game. Traveling to locations and resting deplete a special counter; when it reaches zero, the apocalypse is triggered and the game is over. It is necessary to battle the antagonists and advance the plot in order to reset the counter.

197152.overview: Oh! Pai is an adaptation of a tile game that has similarities to mahjong, though with much simpler rules. The player competes one-on-one against any of the six young women featured in the game. Each opponent offers a different thematic set of tiles (e.g. a stereotypical shy schoolgirl uses teddy bears, pink clothes, etc.), but the game rules are always the same: form simple combinations of three or more identical tiles to win. After each successful round the girl removed a part of her clothes.
